videos.title: Why the Monkey Has a Word for Every Predator #Shorts

comments.author: @melissaneely3018
comments.replyText: Thank you! It really is remarkable. The fact that scientists could play recordings with no predator present and still get the exact right escape response proves those calls carry real meaning. One of the closest things to language in the animal kingdom.

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Three distinct alarm calls, each means a specific threat
clipCandidates.why: Core reveal — leopard call = run up tree, eagle call = dive into bushes, snake call = stand and scan. Concrete, surprising, easy to visualize.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a monkey has three different words for danger

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Scientists played recordings with no predator, monkeys still did the right move
clipCandidates.why: Proof moment — the calls carry meaning, not just fear. This is the 'aha' that elevates from animal behavior to proto-language.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Scientists proved monkeys have a language

videos.title: Why the Rhino Horn Is Made of Hair Not Bone #Shorts

comments.author: @mandyhixson9815
comments.text: I did not know that that's just amazing
comments.replyText: Thank you so much! It is one of those facts that changes how you see them. A weapon made of the same stuff as your fingernails, and it never stops growing back. Glad you enjoyed it!

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Horn is keratin, same as fingernails and hair, not bone or ivory
clipCandidates.why: Core reveal — most people think rhino horn is bone or ivory. Keratin connection to human body is relatable and surprising.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a rhino horn is made of hair not bone

clipCandidates.momentLabel: If cut above the root, horn regrows 2-3 inches per year
clipCandidates.why: Regeneration payoff — conservation dehorning works because horn regrows. Practical implication makes it memorable.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: A rhino that can grow its horn back
